title: Conditional validity of quantum event classifiers under collider systematics and quantum estimation uncertainty
authors: Roberto Fernández-Barrios, Iker Pastor-López, Asier González-Santocildes, Pablo García Bringas
abstract: Claims about a deployed quantum machine-learning classifier can fail when target data shift or when finite-shot quantum evaluation randomizes the model itself. We develop an information-conditional, fail-closed auditing framework that returns supported, refuted or unresolved verdicts with anytime-valid per-claim error control under a declared sampling protocol. On a Higgs-to-tau-tau collider benchmark, stable classifier metrics do not guarantee valid signal-strength inference: at the studied finite-template statistics, the fixed-template profile can lose coverage, even in shift-free controls, when its templates are estimated independently and template-statistical uncertainty is not modeled explicitly. Across 30 frozen finite-shot quantum-kernel deployments, every realized Gram matrix is propagated through refitting, calibration and threshold selection; in the primary raw pipeline these perturbations leave ranking nearly unchanged yet move thresholded target metrics by about 0.02, flipping ideal-anchored claims, and the diagonal-loading sensitivity decomposes differently. Matched classical controls remove apparent quantum-specific nominal-performance and sensing effects. We claim no quantum advantage.
summary: This work introduces a robust, information-conditional auditing framework to assess whether claims made by Quantum Machine-Learning classifiers remain valid when subjected to real-world systematic uncertainties and finite quantum measurement noise. Using a collider physics benchmark, the authors show that simple classifier performance metrics are insufficient for scientific inference, concluding that no demonstrable quantum advantage exists over classical methods under their rigorous testing protocol.
main_problem: The paper addresses the conditional validity of Quantum Machine-Learning (QML) classifiers when deployed in real-world high-energy physics inference pipelines, considering both classical systematic shifts and quantum measurement uncertainties.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that classifier validity does not guarantee scientific inference validity, and that apparent quantum advantages can be reproduced by matched classical controls, leading them to claim no quantum advantage.
method: They develop an information-conditional, fail-closed auditing framework that rigorously tests claims by propagating results through various information sets ($I_0$ to $I_3$) and accounting for finite-shot quantum estimation noise.

key_observables: Classifier metrics (e.g., AUC), signal-strength coverage, and the status of claims (SUPPORTED, REFUTED, UNRESOLVED) under various systematic variations.

main_assumptions: The framework assumes a 'frozen finite-population batch deployment' snapshot, and the validity guarantee is conditional on the declared sampling protocol and information sets.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the need for information-conditional certification, details the fail-closed auditing framework, applies it to collider data under systematic variations, and concludes by comparing QML results against classical controls to assess true advantage.
why_interesting: While focused on HEP, the rigorous statistical framework for certifying claims under systematic uncertainty and finite sampling is highly relevant to any field using quantum measurements or complex ML models where systematic error control is paramount.

figures.caption: Fig. 1 Framework. The information-set hierarchy I0→I3 and the fail-closed decision rule. Claims about a frozen deployment are audited under declared information; heuristic sensors may veto certifi- cation but never grant it. At I2, fixed label-stream claims carry anytime-valid per-claim error control; I3 and empirical ledgers use separate coverage gates or calibrated tests. Unresolved claims remain UNRESOLVED.

Fig. 2 TES response under the frozen environment grid (five training seeds, development world; ∆AUC = nominal minus shifted AUC, positive = degradation). The TES down-shift sign replicates within this world at the 10−3 scale; the cross-world evaluation later shows that its direction is draw- dependent (§2.4). Adverse combinations are discussed in the text but are not displayed in this panel.
